text:
olivia: Quick heads-up — I'm about to promote an overlay change to prod that adjusts canary routing weights and swaps a couple secrets from SSM paths to SecretManager (k8s secret references). Wanted a quick gating + rollback sanity check before I hit promote.

raj: Thanks. Can you paste the kustomize overlay diff and the terraform plan output? Focused on whether any IAM or secret rotation resources change.

olivia: Pasted below — small kustomize patch and the terraform plan snippet from the infra repo.

olivia: ```diff
@@ overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml
 - namePrefix: prod-
 resources:
 - ../../base
 + # new canary routing config
 + patchesStrategicMerge:
 + - canary-route-patch.yaml
 
 # secret refs
 - secretGenerator:
 - - name: db-credentials
 -   literals:
 -   - DB_USER=redwood
 -   - DB_PASS=secret
 + secretGenerator:
 + - name: db-credentials
 +   behavior: merge
 +   envs:
 +   - ../../secrets/prod/db.env
 ```

olivia: Terraform plan (trimmed):

olivia: ```
Plan: 0 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy.
  ~ aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.db_creds
      secret_id: "arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:123456789012:secret:db-creds-XXXXX" => same
      secret_string: (sensitive value changed)
Note: No IAM role changes.
```

marta: Good call. The change to secret version is expected — you're creating a new version to store rotated payload. Two gating asks:
- Ensure KMS key policy doesn't get unintentionally widened by whatever automation publishes the new secret.
- Confirm canary route patch includes a fallback to primary (100% if canary fails).

sam: For rollback plan: if the new secret version misbehaves, we should be able to roll back by pinning the k8s secretGenerator to the previous env file hash and revert canary weights in the overlay. Suggest adding a small runbook comment in the PR with exact kustomize commands:

sam: ```
# rollback steps (prod)
kubectl -n infra apply -k overlays/prod --record
# to revert canary
kubectl -n infra patch svc redwood-api --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/canaryWeight","value":0}]'
# reapply secrets from previous env
kubectl create secret generic db-credentials --from-env-file=secrets/prod/db.env --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```

raj: Also add the terraform state clear note — if you need to revert secret version publish, we should avoid re-running the plan until we confirm secret contents. i.e., don't reapply TF that would produce another version change.

infra-bot: ci check: infra/overlays/prod PR run passed all lint + kustomize build checks. kustomize build output shows new canary route added.

ci-bot: pipeline: https://ci.redwood.company/teams/infra/pipelines/2981 — integration tests for canary passed in staging-2. Build #2981 succeeded at 2026-03-16T14:12:03Z :thumbsup:

marta: Quick permissions sanity: olivia — can you confirm which principal is publishing the new secret version? is it the deployer service account or the CI runner role? We need to ensure our least-privilege KMS policy remains.

olivia: It's the deployer role (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/deployer-prod). CI only creates the TF plan; deployer executes the apply. I checked KMS policy — no widen detected in the plan; infra-bot summary concurs.

raj: All good then. One more ask: add a short canary evaluation threshold in the overlay (error-rate < 1% & p95 latency within 10% of baseline) and an automated rollback hook if thresholds breach within 30m. Can you include those as annotations in the canary patch?

olivia: Yep — will add annotations and a runbook snippet in the PR. I'll wait ~30m for any final objections then promote. tagging @marta @sam for visibility.

marta: No objections from me. :+1:

sam: LGTM once annotations + runbook added. I'll watch the canary rollout.

olivia: Thanks all — promoting in ~25m unless something pops up. infra-bot, please watch the deploy and ping here if KMS/SecretsManager errors show up.

infra-bot: Acknowledged. Will post status updates on failures or IAM/KMS errors.
